env_render — DRIVE env op

• Data kinds: table × matrix × matrix → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.env_render(world: 'dict', pose, K, width: 'int' = 640, height: 'int' = 400, env: 'Optional[dict]' = None, *, ego=None, ego_pose=None, shadows: 'bool' = True, shadow_cache: 'Optional[dict]' = None, shadow_res: 'int' = 1024) -> 'Dict[str, np.ndarray]' (to call the implementation directly, import driveenv; driveenv.env_render(world: 'dict', pose, K, width: 'int' = 640, height: 'int' = 400, env: 'Optional[dict]' = None, *, ego=None, ego_pose=None, shadows: 'bool' = True, shadow_cache: 'Optional[dict]' = None, shadow_res: 'int' = 1024) -> 'Dict[str, np.ndarray]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("env_render"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Renders sun, sky, shadows, lamps, headlights, fog, rain and glare in physical units.

Returns

dict : color (camera linear RGB [0,1], compressed by tone_map —— image processing reads this), display (sRGB-encoded,

for display, used only for figures), radiance (RGB luminance cd/m², linear), depth, label, face (same as driveworld.world_camera), shadow (bool, pixels in sun shadow), exposure (multiplier used), veil (veiling luminance cd/m² (H,W)), illuminance (surface illuminance lx (H,W)).

ego_pose=(x, y, yaw) = pose of the ego vehicle carrying the headlamps (2 lamps at front end 2.25 m, ±0.6 m left/right, height 0.65 m). Passing a dict to shadow_cache reuses the sun's shadow map (as long as the sun and the world do not change).

Empty input (world is an empty dict) raises ValueError.
